chunks: And do not take a life, which God has forbidden, except in a just cause. We have given the right (of redress) to the heir of the person who is killed, but he should not exceed the limits (of justice) by slaying (the killer), for he will be judged (by the same law).
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for taking a life according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'wali' is often interpreted broadly to include the Imam or the victim himself, emphasizing the divine authority granted to seek justice (qisas) or compensation (diyah). This verse underscores the sanctity of life as a fundamental right, linking the preservation of individual souls to the maintenance of social order and legal equity under divine sanction.
